(BY SHRI RAKESH KUMAR JAIN - ADVOCATE FOR THE RESPOND  NO.3 )
 __________________________________________________________  This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court   following:
 ORDER
With the consent of the parties, the matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 24.06.2023 passed in MACC.No.548/2022 5th Additional M.A.C.T., Mandla District- Mandla seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.3,000/- treating her as household lady.

Learned counsel for the appellants, after relying upon Laxmidhar Nayak and Ors. Vs. Jugal Kishore Behera and ors. 2018 (1) SCC 746,
Ram Singh vs Munna Lal on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107382560/
2 submits that if deceased's income is determined treating her as an unskilled labour, then, 50%

entities.text: Laxmidhar Nayak and Ors. Vs. Jugal Kishore Behera and ors. 2018 (1) SCC 746
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: should
be added for household work and if deceased income is determined treating her as skilled labour, then, it may be determined as per income of skilled person on the date of accident
. It is also urged that Tribunal has not added 10% to the amount of consortium as per in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157,

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just & proper.
No enhancement is required.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. So far as income of deceased is concerned, admittedly, Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.3,000/- per month.
Evidently, deceased was an household lady and as per submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants, she was also working as labourer,

Therefore, in view of law laid down in Arvind Kumar Pandey & Ors. Vs. Girish Pandey & Anr in Civil Appeal No.2512 of 2024 (Arising out of SLP(C) No.20918 of 2022), it would be proper to determine deceased's monthly income treating her as skilled person.

entities.text: Arvind Kumar Pandey & Ors. Vs. Girish Pandey & Anr in Civil Appeal No.2512 of 2024 (Arising out of
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On date of accident, minimum wages of a skilled person were Rs.11,360/-.

Therefore, deceased's monthly income is determined as Rs.11,360/-
per month.
In view of age of deceased, 40% is to be added as future prospect and multiplier of 16 is to be applied.
Further, in view of number of dependent, one third is to be deducted for personal and living expenses.
7. Perusal of para-23 of impugned award reveals that Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- to each appellant as consortium.

In view of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157 and taking into consideration the date of accident, each appellant is entitled to receive Rs.44,000/- as consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal has awarded Rs.16,500/- each for funeral expenses and loss of estate.

8. Hence, in view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-
 S.No. Heads   1. Monthly Income of the appellant   2. Additional Future prospect 40% 
 3.

Monthly loss of dependency (1/3rd) 
 4. Annual loss of dependency   6. Multiplier of 16  7. Compensation for loss of spousal/parental/filial Rs. 1,32,000/-
consortium 9.

Compensation for loss of estate and towards Rs.33,000/-
funeral expenses Ram Singh vs Munna Lal on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107382560/
3 10. Medical expenses Nil 11.

Total Compensation Rs.22,01,544/-
12.

Total compensation awarded by the Tribunal Rs.6,90,000/-
13.

Actual Enhancement Rs.15,11,544/-
9.
Hence, in view of above, in the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and proper to enhance compensation Rs.15,11,544/-.
10. Enhanced compensation Rs.15,11,544/- shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
11. Appellants have valued present appeal for Rs.10,33,000/- and has paid court fees accordingly.
Therefore, appellants shall be entitled to receive enhanced amount only after payment of deficit court fees.

12. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance company submits that en-1.
hancement of compensation should be to the extent to which appellants have paid Court fees and if there is any deficit Court fees, then, before deciding the appeal, appellants be directed to pay deficit Court fees and accordingly value the appeal.

With respect to above, learned counsel for the appellants has relied upon M.A.No.155 of 2019 (Manoj Kumar & Others Vs. H.D.F.C. and Others)
decided on 17.04.2023.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar & Others Vs. H.D.F.C. and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in para-12 has held as under:-
"12.

Thus, the question as to whether the Court fee is payable at the time of presenta- tion of appeal or at the time of final hearing of the appeal or after the adjudication of just compensation has already been decided and it has been held that the Court Fee is payable at the time of presentation of ap- peal."
13.
In this Court's opinion, there is no dispute with respect to above preposition of law.

But in above case, no issue was raised before co-ordinate Bench that if an appeal has been valued and Courts fees has been paid accordingly, but later- on, at the time of deciding the same, Court finds that appellant is entitled to re- ceive more compensation, then, the valuation of appeal.
What would be the procedure in such case.
14. In the instant case, present appeal has been valued for Rs.10,33,000/- and this Court has found that appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.15,11,541/-.
Therefore, it cannot be said that appellants has grossly under- valued appeal and on above grounds, just and proper compensation cannot be denied.
15. Hence, above submissions of learned counsel for the Insurance Company are rejected.
